name: Audible Premium Plus
subcategory: music services and creator audio tools
tagline: Organize and play legally owned audiobooks with bookmarks and local sync

pricing.notes: Official US monthly Premium Plus rate.

tiers.name: Audible Standard
tiers.limits: 1 selected audiobook/month from 1 million+ eligible titles; 0 Plus Catalog access.

tiers.name: Premium Plus Annual, 12 Credits
tiers.limits: 12 credits issued upfront; Plus Catalog access.

tiers.name: Premium Plus Annual, 24 Credits
tiers.limits: 24 credits issued upfront; Plus Catalog access.

pricing.billingTerms: Monthly + annual; annual plans issue all 12 or 24 credits upfront. A 30-day trial is promotional, not a permanent free tier.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Unused credits expire 12 months after issue; extra credit packs cost extra; Plus Catalog titles disappear after cancellation, while titles purchased with credits remain in the library.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Audible Premium Plus, organize and play legally owned audiobooks with bookmarks and local sync. The hard boundary is licensed audiobook catalog, credits, publisher relationships, narration rights, and apps, plus licensed content, rights, and distribution network.
coreLoopDIY: Organize legally owned audiobooks, play them with bookmarks, sync listening progress locally, and keep the library in a private user-owned store.
whatYouLose: licensed audiobook catalog, credits, publisher relationships, narration rights, and apps
moatNotes: licensed content, rights, and distribution network
ongoingBurden: catalog licensing, royalties, identity, content delivery, moderation, recommendations, payouts, codecs, and rights disputes
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Audible Premium Plus because the product is the catalog, rights chain, and distribution network; a player or processing tool is only the visible edge. The recurring cost buys catalog licensing, royalties, identity, content delivery, moderation, recommendations, payouts, codecs, and rights disputes, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Navidrome
priorArt.desc: Active open-source personal music server for legally owned libraries.

alternatives.name: Audiobookshelf
alternatives.desc: Your audiobooks, bookmarks and progress on your server; the giant licensed catalogue stays gone.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium Plus plan and a personal library or creator utility DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Audible Premium Plus in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, ffmpeg, and a local web interface; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize legally owned audiobooks, play them with bookmarks, sync listening progress locally, and keep the library in a private user-owned store.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Index only user-selected folders and preserve source audio without modification.
Read tags and artwork, calculate loudness and waveform data, and detect exact duplicates by hash.
Provide albums, artists, playlists, search, queue, favorites, and resumable local playback.
Add optional creator tools for trim, normalize, split stems through a local model, and export new files.
Keep all rights and source information attached to imported tracks and display it during export.
Document that the application does not provide music, licensing, distribution, or royalty collection.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out copyrighted catalog acquisition or sharing.
Deliberately leave out streaming-service circumvention.
Deliberately leave out royalty accounting, label distribution, and global content delivery.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
